fig1_legendre.svg: Legendre polynomials $P_1$–$P_4$ on $[-1,1]$ from legendre (the recurrence $(n+1)P_{n+1}=(2n+1)xP_n-nP_{n-1}$). Each $P_n$ has $n$ zeros and definite parity $P_n(-x)=(-1)^n P_n(x)$, with $P_n(1)=1$; they are the orthogonal SL eigenfunctions of the polar-angle equation $-((1-x^2)y')'=n(n+1)y$ that build the multipole expansion.
fig2_bessel.svg: Bessel functions $J_0$–$J_3$ from bessel_j, evaluated by the integral representation $J_n(x)=\frac1\pi\int_0^\pi\cos(n\tau-x\sin\tau)\,d\tau$. They solve $x^2y''+xy'+(x^2-n^2)y=0$ and oscillate with slowly decaying amplitude ($J_0(0)=1$, $J_{n\ge1}(0)=0$); their zeros set the radial drum and waveguide modes, orthogonal under the weight $w=x$.
